subject: Hosted API — data evacuation, retention windows, and deletion timelines
messages:
From: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@alderpay.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AlderPay Security Team <security@alderpay.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AlderPay security questionnaire — residency and deletion clarifications

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for sending your completed questionnaire. A few follow-ups from our InfoSec review around data residency, retention, and deletion for the Hosted API:

1) In your matrix you list "ephemeral caching" and "longer-term logs" separately. Can you confirm the maximum retention windows for: request/response cache, request metadata (headers, timestamps), and aggregated usage logs?

2) If AlderPay needs a full account wipe (tenant deletion), what is the typical timeline for: a) removing data from live serving clusters, b) sanitizing backups, and c) removing analytics/aggregation artifacts?

3) Do you offer a written attestation or exported report showing that data tied to a tenant identifier has been deleted from all hosted systems? If so, what format and what SLA?

I've attached the questionnaire with our flags (AlderPay_Security_Q_v3.xlsx). We need answers by end of day Friday to keep procurement on schedule.

Best,
Claire

Claire Dunn
Senior Security Analyst, AlderPay
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: AlderPay security questionnaire — residency and deletion clarifications

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear questions. Below are concise, source-level answers; I flagged two items for an engineering confirm and looped in Marissa (security) and Diego (platform) for detail and evidence links.

1) Retention windows (hosted API):
- Request/response cache (prefix KV & request-level ephemeral cache): default TTL is 2 minutes; configurable per-customer up to 6 hours via routing policy. Cache is in-memory on serving nodes and evicted on restart.
- Request metadata (ingest metadata like headers, timestamps): retained for 30 days by default for troubleshooting; customers can request a shorter TTL (minimum 0 days) at account level.
- Aggregated usage logs (per-token billing, aggregated latency histograms): retained for 13 months for billing/analytics. We can provide shorter retention windows for enterprise contracts.

2) Account wipe (tenant deletion) timeline:
- a) Live serving clusters: when a tenant deletion is initiated, routing entries are removed immediately (within <5 minutes) and new requests return 404/tenant-not-found. Active in-flight requests complete but no new requests are accepted.
- b) Backups & persisted snapshots: routine backups are retained as described in our retention matrix; sanitized deletion from backups is a two-step process: logical deletion is applied immediately and physical removal from cold backup storage begins within 30 days; complete purging from long-term backup media may take up to 90 days depending on the storage tier.
- c) Analytics/aggregates: aggregated artifacts that cannot be tied back to raw tenant identifiers are re-computed on a rolling window; artifacts that contain tenant identifiers are scheduled for purge within 30 days.

3) Deletion attestation and export:
- We provide a signed deletion attestation PDF that includes the tenant id, deletion request id, timestamps for logical and physical deletion phases, and list of locations scoped (primary clusters, backup buckets, analytics). Standard SLA for attestation delivery: 7 business days after completion of the physical purge. For accelerated timelines or legal hold scenarios we can negotiate shorter SLA in the contract.

Evidence and links: I am attaching an evidence pack (redwood_evidence_pack_v2.zip) with our retention matrix and deletion playbook excerpts. Marissa — can you confirm the attestation format and the 7-business-day SLA? Diego — can you confirm the physical purge windows for cold backups (30–90 days) and whether we can commit to an explicit 45-day purge for AlderPay if required?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

2) Cold backup encryption: can we offer customer-segregated KMS keys (US region) for AlderPay backups, or if we cannot, what are the access controls and audit paths for the shared keys? Also, if we offer a segregated key, what's the typical lead time and any cost impact?

Subject: Re: FW: AlderPay security questionnaire — residency and deletion clarifications

Stephanie / Claire / Marissa — quick engineering confirmations below.

1) Metadata=0: We will stop persisting request metadata to durable stores when a customer requests 0 days. Transient metadata may exist in process memory during request handling and in ephemeral system logs (rotating node logs) for up to the node's configured log-rotation window (default 24 hours). Those node logs are not replicated to durable long-term storage unless a customer-support ticket explicitly requests collection for debugging; in that case we obtain explicit approval. In short: no persistent write to tenant-linked durable stores when retention=0; ephemeral in-memory traces and short-lived node logs (up to 24h) may exist.

2) Cold backup encryption: We support two models for Hosted API backups in the US region:
- Shared KMS (default): backups are encrypted with company-managed keys; access is tightly role-restricted and audited (IAM roles + key access logs retained 13 months).
- Customer-managed KMS (optional enterprise add-on): we can provision customer-segregated KMS keys (AlderPay-managed or customer-supplied keys) for cold backups. Lead time: typically 7–10 business days to configure and test; there may be additional charges for key management and cross-account attestations which we'll surface in the SOW.

If AlderPay wants the customer-managed KMS model, we can include it in the order form and commit to key segregation for the specified US region.

Diego

Claire — looping back with confirmations from engineering:

• Metadata retention = 0: No writes to tenant-durable stores. Transient in-memory traces and rotating node logs (default maximum 24 hours) may exist; we do not replicate those to long-term durable stores unless explicitly requested for debug and approved.
• Cold backups: we support customer-managed KMS for cold backups in the US region (7–10 business day lead time, potential add-on charges). Otherwise we use tightly-restricted, company-managed keys with full key-access audit logs.

I've attached the final evidence pack (redwood_evidence_pack_v2.zip) and added a short deletion attestation template; if AlderPay approves customer-managed KMS in their order form we will include the KMS configuration and lead time in the SOW.

If you'd like this in a signed attestation PDF, Marissa can produce the 7-business-day attestation after physical purge completes. Are you okay with the node-log caveat (24-hour max) and the 7–10 business day KMS lead time?

Thanks — happy to finalize.
